lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- What Should HR Do Now?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Viviane Rodrigues de Oliveira | Lesson 10 -- What Should HR Do Now?
lesson.grammar_point: modals of recommendation should ought to had better

listenings.text: I spent years giving advice nobody used, and I finally understood why. I was giving the board a list. Six recommendations, all of them sensible, and the meeting always ended the same way: interesting, let us come back to this. Now I do the opposite. One recommendation. The one I would defend if they only did one thing. And three sentences: what we should do, why, and what happens if we wait. That last part changed everything. Before, my advice was a good idea. Now it has a cost attached to doing nothing, and a board can act on that. One more thing I learned the hard way. Do not say must when you mean should. Save must for the audit and the law. If everything is must, nothing is, and after two or three of those they stop listening to you completely.

I want to say something to the candidates who write to me and apologise for their English before they even start. Almost every senior person I hire is working in their second language, and almost none of them speak it perfectly. What I need is different. I need you to understand my question, ask me to repeat it when you do not, and answer with something concrete. That is it. I have never rejected anybody for an accent or for a wrong verb. I have rejected many people for pretending they understood, and for answering a question I did not ask. And here is the part nobody tells you. The candidates who say I am still learning, and here is where I am, sound more senior than the ones who pretend. Confidence in an interview is not perfect grammar. It is being comfortable with what you do not know yet.

extra_audio.text: I would recommend starting with the north region. It has the lowest retention, and the root cause is the first month. If we wait until September, we should expect to lose two more managers. So I need approval for two trainers from May.

paras: This memo has three recommendations and one thing we should not do. The problem is known: store retention in the north region, with the first thirty days as the root cause.

First, we should put two trainers in the north region from May. Second, we should change the onboarding guideline so that every new person has a one-to-one with their manager in week one. That is a quick win and it costs nothing. Third, we must review the overtime policy, because compliance flagged it last month and that one is not optional.
What we should not do is launch all four regions at the same time. We do not have enough trainers, and a rollout without owners is a plan that looks good in a slide and dies in June.

The risk of waiting is not theoretical. If we start in the next quarter instead of May, we should expect to lose two or three more store managers, and each one costs us about three months of hiring and training. My recommendation is to approve the two trainers now and review the rest in September.
